references.text: This verse introduces the instructions for the offerings during the Feast of Tabernacles, where the number of bulls decreases by one each day, culminating in the eight bulls mentioned on the sixth day.
These verses provide the context for the Feast of Tabernacles and the specific offering pattern with a decreasing number of bulls over the seven days of the festival.
The requirement that the animals be without blemish (תְּמִימִם) is repeated here, as in all offering instructions.
This text in Leviticus describes the Feast of Tabernacles, which lasts for seven days and is the same festival to which the offerings in Numbers 29 belong.
The daily burnt offering that forms the basis for the additional festival offerings, including those mentioned on the sixth day of the Feast of Tabernacles.
